forecast-period.text: A trough of low pressure that lies near the NT/WA border will combine with a trough and cold front further south to move over much of SA on Saturday, and over the far northeast on Sunday. A ridge of high pressure will then move into the west from late Sunday and persist over the rest of the state throughout next week.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Showers and possible thunderstorms in the south, extending broadly across the state during the afternoon and tending to rain at times. Severe thunderstorms are possible with risk of damaging wind gusts and large hail mainly about the northern agricultural area and adjacent parts. Maximum temperatures above average, grading to below average in the far southwest. Southeast to northeasterly winds at first, tending to north to northwesterly winds ahead of a fresh and gusty south to southwesterly change extending throughout the day.

Showers and possible thunderstorms, contracting northeastwards during the day. Showers likely to redevelop and continue about the agricultural areas. Severe thunderstorms with damaging wind gusts may be possible about the far northeast in the afternoon. Maximum temperatures below average, grading to well below average in the northwest. Fresh and gusty south to southwesterly winds, easing from the evening and tending south to southeasterly in the west.

Showers about the agricultural areas and western coasts. Isolated showers and possible thunderstorms about the far northwest. Maximum temperatures below average. South to southwesterly winds, tending southeasterly in the north and in the west later.

text.p: Isolated showers about the southern agricultural area. Isolated showers and possible thunderstorms about the north and west. Maximum temperatures below average. Southwest to southeasterly winds.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Tuesday: 2 to 10 mm broadly across SA. Possible falls of 10 to 20 mm about parts of the agricultural areas, ranges and western coasts, with localised falls of 20 to 30 mm also possible. Heavier falls between 20 to 50 mm are possible with thunderstorms.
